title: Approach2: run Neo4j docker import + verify
description: Docker daemon must be running; then run ./approach2-using-existing-graph/scripts/neo4j_up_and_import.sh and verify data in Neo4j Browser (http://localhost:7474).
notes: Ports aligned to 7474/7687 in helper script

title: Feature: Deterministic risk report from user-provided Azure resource identity (no Terraform plan)
description:
Replace Terraform plan-driven workflows with a user-driven workflow where the user specifies the Azure resource being changed (resource ID and/or name+type+scope). The system resolves that input to a single graph entity in Neo4j, gathers bounded/allowlisted evidence, applies deterministic scoring rules, and outputs a reproducible risk report.

Scope:
- Inputs: Azure Resource ID OR (name + resource type + subscription + resource group) with interactive disambiguation.
- Entity resolution: deterministic, explicit tie-breakers, and clear errors.
- Evidence: only from allowlisted Cypher templates with strict bounds (limits/timeouts/max-hop/max-results) and no user-supplied Cypher.
- Output: deterministic ordering and stable report format.

Non-goals:
- Terraform plan parsing/integration.
- Auto-discovery of “what changed” beyond the provided resource identity.
acceptance_criteria:
- CLI accepts user-provided resource identity and produces a risk report for that entity.
- Same inputs against same DB snapshot yield identical score and evidence ordering.
- Neo4j access is via allowlisted, bounded queries only; no arbitrary Cypher execution.
- Clear UX for invalid/ambiguous inputs, with non-interactive mode support.

title: CLI: accept Azure resource identity via flags + interactive prompts
description:
Define the user input contract for identifying the resource being changed. Support:
- `--resource-id` (preferred)
- Or `--resource-name`, `--resource-type`, `--subscription-id`, `--resource-group`
- `--non-interactive` mode (fail fast on missing/ambiguous)
- Interactive prompts when required fields are missing or ambiguity exists.

Deliver a single canonical “ResourceSpec” structure for downstream steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- Running the CLI with `--resource-id` proceeds without prompts.
- Running without required fields triggers prompts in interactive mode and errors in `--non-interactive`.
- A canonical parsed `ResourceSpec` is produced with normalized casing and validated required fields.

title: Input validation: parse/normalize Azure Resource ID and resource type
description:
Implement strict validation and normalization for Azure identifiers.

Key behaviors:
- Parse Azure Resource ID into components (subscription, resource group, provider namespace, type segments, name segments).
- Normalize resource type to canonical form (e.g., `Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines`).
- Validate allowed characters/lengths; reject obviously invalid IDs early.
- Provide actionable error messages (what’s missing/invalid).

Note: This task is purely input-side; graph resolution happens separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Valid Azure Resource IDs are parsed into structured components.
- Invalid IDs (missing segments, wrong prefix, illegal chars) are rejected with clear messages.
- Resource type normalization is deterministic and documented (examples covered).

title: Approach2: Deterministic agent-derived risk report
description: Implement deterministic risk scoring + structured Markdown reporting via the Risk Assessment agent using the Neo4j MCP server (no standalone CLI).
acceptance_criteria:
- Using the Risk Assessment agent + Neo4j MCP, assessing a Service/AzureResource/Subscription returns a single Markdown report
- Report includes: resolved entity table, evidence summary table, derived relationship map, score breakdown table, and top-N evidence tables
- Score is deterministic given the same graph state (stable sorting, integer rubric, no randomness, no time-based drift unless asked)
- Approach 2 README points to agent usage/prompt
close_reason: Aligned to agent+Neo4j MCP (structured Markdown + deterministic rubric) and removed standalone CLI.

title: Risk Assessment Agent: structured markdown output
description: Update the Risk Assessment Agent instructions to require structured Markdown output (tables) and an explicit deterministic scoring rubric aligned with the CLI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent output format specifies Markdown sections and tables
- Sorting/formatting rules documented to reduce variability
- Scoring rubric defined as deterministic integer math with caps/thresholds
close_reason: Updated Risk Assessment Agent instructions for structured Markdown output and deterministic scoring/ordering rules.
